title: the WSG portable shelters slice with Table 36 - the simple pole-and-cloth shelter with the pitch rules, the occupancy limits, the four-band quality-by-size characteristics grid and the p. 61 cave-sentence seam tail, printed p. 62
audit_label: R472 WSG portable shelters pin audit
audit_comment: The Table 36 grid (the four-quality-band by three-size portable shelter characteristics: encumbrance value, cost, setup time dice, moisture tier, wind resistance, life span), the simple shelter mechanics (the 6-10 foot pole, the waterproof cloth, the 30-45 degree pitch, the ropes and stakes, the opening away from the wind), the occupancy limits (one human, two smaller characters, two men in a pinch), the hauling rules and the p. 61 cave-slope seam tail - every const, bool and table cell verified against the model.

banner.title: R472: the WSG PORTABLE SHELTERS slice with TABLE 36 - the p. 61 seam tail (a cave in the face of a mountain slope is a superior shelter in all respects, assuming the opening faces away from the wind; the Dungeon Master judgment prevailing in any circumstances not covered), the portable shelter basics (characters mindful of the need for shelter carrying the appropriate materials; a single mount or size M pack animal easily transporting all the gear for many shelter types with plenty of carrying capacity left over; in the absence of an animal a single average-strength character hauling on his back enough for himself and a small group at their rest stops), the simplest form (a single wooden pole of 6-10 feet plus a fairly large expanse of heavy, waterproofed cloth or similarly pliable material; the DM may allow a two- or three-piece pole apparatus held by lashings or pegs, easier to transport), the pitch rules (the pole anchored at 30 to 45 degrees, one end braced on the ground and the other a few feet in the air, the covering draped over the pole, the edges touching the ground or tied down with ropes and stakes, the opening facing opposite the wind), the occupancy (enough space for one human or a pair of smaller characters, and in a pinch two men with no appreciable loss of protection or comfort), the escalation (more elaborate and larger shelters necessary for especially vicious weather or a decent-sized group huddling in one tent) and Table 36 PORTABLE SHELTER CHARACTERISTICS: the four quality bands poor, adequate, good, superior by small, medium, large - encumbrance value 350/450/600, 500/600/750, 600/800/1000, 750/1000/1500; cost 10/20/30, 30/50/75, 75/120/180, 200/300/400 gold pieces; setup time 1d2+1/1d2+2/1d2+3, 1d3+1/1d3+2/1d3+3, 1d3+1/1d3+2/1d4+2, 1d4+1/1d4+2/1d4+3 turns; moisture resistance light, moderate, heavy, downpour; wind resistance 20/30/40/50 percent; life span 40/80/120/180 days), printed p. 62.
banner.provenance: Ground truth two-way, no contested cells, no physical-page reads: the R467 TSV-GEOMETRY WORKFLOW (the uploaded p62_tsv.tsv word boxes, the twelve-row grid rebuilt from the bounding geometry) vs the user-run Termux tesseract text of printed p. 62 (p62_full.txt). The two readers AGREE ON ALL 72 GRID CELLS (twelve rows by six columns). The pdf text layer (p62_pdfy.txt) is the third reader: it garbles the dice glyphs as ld (the known pattern) but agrees on every value and on all prose numbers - the 6-10 foot pole, the 30-45 degree pitch, the one-human occupancy with the pair-of-smaller and two-men-in-a-pinch readings. The GOOD LARGE SETUP OUTLIER 1d4+2 (breaking the 1d3+ pattern of its band) is verified in all three readers. The p. 61 seam tail (the cave sentence completing the p. 61 shelter-quality guidelines) opens the page.
banner.sentinel: All 72 Table 36 cells pinned (the setup time dice split into a die and a modifier column, the moisture resistance encoded as a four-step tier); the simple-shelter mechanics, the occupancy limits and the hauling rules are audit examples.

consts.name: wpsPoleMinFeet
consts.comment: the simplest portable shelter uses a single wooden pole of 6-10 feet: the length floor

consts.name: wpsPitchMinAngle

bools.name: wpsCaveSlopeSuperior
bools.comment: a cave in the face of a mountain slope is a superior shelter in all respects, assuming the opening faces away from the wind - the p. 61 seam tail

bools.name: wpsDmJudgmentPrevails
bools.comment: the Dungeon Master judgment will prevail in any circumstances not covered by the shelter guidelines

bools.name: wpsMindfulCarryGear
bools.comment: characters properly mindful of the need for good shelter in the wilderness will carry the appropriate materials with them

bools.name: wpsPackAnimalHauls
bools.comment: a single mount or size M pack animal can easily transport all the gear needed for many types of shelters with plenty of carrying capacity left over

bools.name: wpsAvgCharHauls
bools.comment: in the absence of an animal, a single character of average strength can usually haul on his back enough shelter materials to keep himself and a small group of companions comfortable during their rest stops

bools.name: wpsWaterproofClothCover
bools.comment: in its simplest form a portable shelter is a single pole plus a fairly large expanse of heavy, waterproofed cloth or some similarly pliable material

bools.name: wpsMultiPiecePole
bools.comment: the DM may decide the framework pole need not be a single piece but a two- or three-piece apparatus with the parts held together by lashings or pegs when assembled

bools.name: wpsPitchAwayFromWind
bools.comment: to pitch a simple tent the pole is braced at 30 to 45 degrees, the covering draped over it, the edges tied down with ropes and stakes, and the opening in front facing opposite the direction the wind is coming from

bools.name: wpsSimpleFitsOneHuman
bools.comment: this kind of simple shelter provides enough space for one human or a pair of smaller characters

bools.name: wpsTwoMenInPinch
bools.comment: in a pinch two men can use the simple shelter with no appreciable loss of protection or comfort

bools.name: wpsElaborateForVicious
bools.comment: more elaborate and larger shelters are necessary if the weather is especially vicious or if all the characters in a decent-sized group intend to huddle inside the same tent

bools.name: wpsCategoryByQualityAndCapacity
bools.comment: for game purposes portable shelters come in categories related to the quality of protection they provide and the number of man-sized characters they can comfortably contain

prev_record: - R471 LANDED 2026-10-15: commit 2eec600 (census 396, pushed
31f9a0f..2eec600), the WSG NATURAL SHELTERS slice with
TABLE 35, printed p. 61 - the CAMPING AND CAMPFIRES arc
opener (pp. 61-68) and the FIRST TABLE ROUND since R467:
the Table 35 grid (the chance of finding natural shelter
or easily obtainable construction materials, the
six-terrain by four-season percentage grid: Desert
Mountains constant 40, Plains 30/40/40/30, Swamp
40/50/50/40), the check discipline (the DM checks
whenever characters indicate they are looking; a failed
check with the party still moving allows rechecks at
three-turn intervals until shelter is found or they stop
and camp unsheltered), the forest construction rules
(boughs or branches cut and laid across a grid of poles
for a roof and, properly positioned, wind-and-precip
protection; pack animals needing a negotiable path into
closely packed vegetation; 3-8 turns - 1d6+2 - of
material time for a single character, minus 2 turns per
additional helper down to a minimum of 3, then another 6
turns to lash the poles and bind the shingles, minus 1
turn per helper to a maximum of two helpers, the whole
construction time halved with a rope use proficiency
character among the workers), the terrain notes (the
desert surface irregularities - large rocks, small
crevasses, a steeply sloping sand dune - sheltering at
least one side; the hills windbreak with spring-through-
autumn greenery; the mountains read as rough rocky areas
whose table entries model natural features - a cave,
alcove or chimney between rock faces - where the wind
cannot get inside; the plains gully two or three feet
deep but the worst shelter in heavy rain, the non-lush
material time 7-12 turns vs the 3-8 forest; the swamp
debris pile or fallen tree as shelter or foundation) and
the shelter-quality guidelines (many small vegetation
pieces: poor, at best adequate; few large sturdy pieces:
adequate or perhaps good; the lee side of a large rock:
good wind but only adequate-or-poor precip protection -
the prose seams mid-sentence onto p. 62 at the cave
sentence). rules/wsgshelter.h NEW (31 inlines: 11 consts
- wnsTerrainCount 6, the 3/8 forest band, the 2/1 helper
reductions with the 3-turn floor and the 2-helper lash
cap, the 6-turn lashing, the 7/12 plains band, the
3-turn recheck - plus 16 bools plus the four Table 35
season columns, prefix wns, checked free). GROUND TRUTH
